result.summary: A narrow residential lane with sidewalks on both sides, where the constrained street width naturally limits vehicle speeds. Pedestrian space is somewhat compromised by residential encroachments like furniture and potted plants.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A rocking chair and several potted plants are placed on the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking path.

interventions.title: Maintain Clear Walkway
interventions.description: Ensure a continuous clear path of at least 4 feet by removing or relocating private furniture and plants from the public right-of-way.

interventions.title: Shared Street Conversion
interventions.description: Redesign the street as a shared space (Woonerf) with flush curbs and high-quality paving to prioritize pedestrians in this narrow corridor.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow, paved residential alleyway or small street with buildings directly abutting the walkway. The environment is intimate and low-speed, featuring private gates and potted plants that slightly narrow the available walking path.

hazards.name: Walkway Obstructions
hazards.description: Potted plants and containers are placed on the paved walkway, narrowing the clear path for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, along the base of the walls and gates

interventions.title: Clear Path Maintenance
interventions.description: Ensure a consistent clear width is maintained on the walkway by regulating the placement of private planters and decorative items.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install additional wall-mounted lighting to ensure the narrow passage is well-lit and safe for pedestrians at night.

result.summary: A narrow residential alleyway with constrained sidewalks on both sides, leading to a stop-controlled T-junction. The extremely narrow roadway width acts as a natural traffic calming measure, but the pedestrian environment is hampered by sidewalk obstructions and a lack of formal crossing infrastructure at the intersection.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Large storage bins and potted plants on the left sidewalk significantly narrow the available walking space, potentially forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground along the building wall

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt in the roadway and along the sidewalk edges presents a trip hazard.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The junction at the end of the alley lacks a marked crosswalk, reducing pedestrian visibility and priority when crossing the larger street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearance
interventions.description: Enforce regulations to remove private storage containers and large plants from the narrow public walkway to maintain a clear path.

interventions.title: Intersection Enhancements
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk and ADA-compliant curb ramps where the alley meets the cross street.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and level the roadway and sidewalk surfaces to eliminate trip hazards and improve accessibility.

result.summary: The image shows a very narrow residential sidewalk that is significantly obstructed by a large wooden utility pole and the brick steps of a building. This configuration severely restricts the clear walking path, creating a constrained environment for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is positioned in the center of the narrow sidewalk, blocking the majority of the clear walking path.

hazards.name: Narrow Clear Path
hazards.description: The combination of the building's brick steps and the utility pole leaves an insufficient width for safe pedestrian passage.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole to the curb line or underground the utilities to provide a continuous, unobstructed pedestrian through-zone.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Increase the sidewalk width to meet ADA standards, potentially by reallocating space from the roadway if feasible.
